Add the transport note to RestaurantOptions

Spec header bump and section 13 rule
Done
What I found
I reconstructed the working tree from dump.txt (321 files, 319 SHA-256 matches — the two that differ are export.sh, which contains a nested # FILE: marker in its own body, and the last file in the dump, which I trimmed of the footer and then verified to match). The tree is green at Slice 24: 1051 tests, 15 E2E scenarios, all eight local gates passing.

Then I read the tree against what a first tag would make true, and found a real defect.

F-50 — the one variable that discharges the licence is the one variable the stack does not pass.

compose.yaml's web service enumerates its environment key by key and takes no env_file. I ran a census of every environment key the application reads against that block:

APP READS BUT COMPOSE web DOES NOT PASS: ['RESTAURANT_SOURCE_URL']
That is the only one, and it is the worst possible one. F-39 shipped /source as the AGPL §13 remote-interaction offer; OPERATIONS.md §15 is titled "If you fork this — your obligations, and the one variable that meets them" and tells an operator to set exactly this variable in .env. RestaurantOptions.SourceUrl falls back to DefaultSourceUrl = "https://github.com/kusl/myrestaurant".

So: a fork operator who modified the program, set RESTAURANT_SOURCE_URL as instructed, and deployed through the only path this project documents, published an AGPL §13 offer pointing every one of their users at this repository instead of their own modified source. No error, no warning, no log line — the page renders, the link works, and it goes to the wrong tree. Four documents agreed and the transport between them dropped the value on the floor. That's F-38's shape, one layer out.

What I verified before writing anything
The key set can be derived rather than listed — parsed out of RestaurantOptions.FromConfiguration with plain string operations (no Regex; the tree contains none, and warnings are errors in CI). It yields exactly 17 keys, no duplicates.
A second independent observation: every variable named in a Validate() refusal message is a variable the binding method actually reads (15 keys, 0 orphans) — so a rename applied to one half and not the other is caught.
.env.example and spec §13 are both complete; only compose.yaml is wrong.
Sensitivity proven by planting damage: dropped a key from .env.example, from §13, renamed a key in Validate() only, and moved a key onto the postgres service instead of web. Each fires on exactly its own assertion and nothing else. The wrong-service plant is the one that matters — it proves the service-boundary parse is doing real work.
A faithful Python port of the finished C# runs against the real tree and reports FAILING ASSERTIONS: ['3_unreachable'] before the fix, clean after.
Where I got to
Written and verified: the new test tests/MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Tests/Configuration/ConfigurationSurfaceTests.cs (5 facts), the compose.yaml fix (passed through with an empty default, deliberately — repeating the upstream URL there would override a fork's own edit to DefaultSourceUrl and reinstate the same failure one layer up), the RestaurantOptions.cs doc-comment recording why, and the spec header bump to v1.10 plus the new §13 transport rule.

Still to write before I can hand you the archive: §16.4's paragraph on the new test, Appendix A's F-50 row, the DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md row, OPERATIONS.md §15's verification step (and a correction to §14, which currently says git tag v1.0.0 and then lists ghcr.io/kusl/myrestaurant:0.6.0 in the same procedure — same drift in release.yml's header comment), the full BUILD_PROGRESS.md, and _CHANGES.md.

I hit the tool limit mid-flight. Say go and I'll finish those and package m6-slice-25-configuration-reaches-the-container.tar.gz — full files only, extracting at the repository root.

Two things I can tell you now about the archive: no files need deleting, and you'll need git add tests/MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Tests/Configuration/ because that directory is new and the gate scripts enumerate via git ls-files. Expected suite after this slice: 1056, up from 1051.

Nine complete files

The one interesting decision
The fix is one line, but the shape of it matters:

yaml
      RESTAURANT_SOURCE_URL: ${RESTAURANT_SOURCE_URL:-}
Empty default, not the upstream URL — asymmetric with RESTAURANT_NAME and RESTAURANT_CURRENCY_CODE beside it, deliberately. RestaurantOptions.DefaultSourceUrl is a fork's natural first edit. A compose file spelling this repository's URL as its own default would silently override that edit — F-50 reintroduced one layer up, in the file that had just been fixed. An empty value reads as unset via IsNullOrWhiteSpace, so the fallback stays decided in exactly one place.

I rejected env_file: .env: it fixes this instance and hands the container POSTGRES_PASSWORD and CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN along with it — F-45's mistake in a different file. The enumerated block was right; it was one line short.

What I proved before packaging
The gate fails on the Slice 24 tree at assertion 3 naming RESTAURANT_SOURCE_URL, and passes on this one — a gate written today that fails on today's tree is the strongest sensitivity proof available. Six planted violations, each caught by exactly the right assertion:

A remove the fix:        3_unreachable  ['RESTAURANT_SOURCE_URL']
B key on postgres:       3_unreachable  ['RESTAURANT_SOURCE_URL']
C dropped from .env:     4_undocumented ['TABLE_JOIN_GRANT_MINUTES']
D renamed in §13:        5_unspecified  ['ARGON2_MEMORY_KIBIBYTES']
E renamed in Validate:   2_orphans      ['RESTAURANT_CURRENCY']
F brand-new setting:     3, 4 and 5 together
B proves the service-boundary parse does real work rather than searching the file. F is the scenario the gate exists for.

Also: the parser written twice (regex, then plain string walk) and compared — same 17 keys, same 15 validated names. MemoryExtensions.IsWhiteSpace confirmed from dotnet/runtime at release/10.0 to return true on an empty span, which the scanner relies on. SpecificationVersionTests re-run: header 1.10, entries descending — and Version.TryParse reads 1.10 as minor ten, so it sorts above 1.9 correctly, checked rather than assumed. Both YAML files parsed with a real parser and the web mapping re-read from the parsed document. Governance gate 3 clean over every delivered file. Every doc edit applied by exact-match replacement asserting the anchor occurs exactly once.

Finally, the archive was extracted over a clean copy of the tree and all five assertions re-run there.

Expected after applying
dotnet test  →  1056 total, 0 failed        (was 1051)
podman-compose --profile production config | grep RESTAURANT_SOURCE_URL
             →  prints a line. Before this slice it printed nothing.
Still open, deliberately: Permissions-Policy (Slice 24's recorded question — folding a security-header judgement into an AGPL-compliance slice would muddy both records), and the two operator actions no tar can contain.
